revise.statement: Working tree differs from HEAD only by CRLF line endings (all files M); no content drift
RequestContext merged into AppContext (deprecated module __getattr__ alias, removal in 4.0); one contextvar _cv_app for all proxies

Behavior change: outer app context no longer reused during request dispatch; per-request appcontext_pushed/popped and teardown_appcontext; g of outer context not visible during request (3.1 reused it)
evidence: git show c2705ffd^:src/flask/ctx.py (3.1 RequestContext.push reuse logic)

revise.statement: 12 Flask dispatch/teardown methods now take ctx first param; __init_subclass__ detects old-signature overrides, warns DeprecationWarning at class-definition time, wraps subclass method (remove_ctx) and globally patches base Flask (add_ctx)
Old-signature compat path (warn+wrap branch) has no direct test coverage; new-signature path covered by test_subclassing.py only
evidence: grep of tests for subclass overrides (8 Flask subclasses, none old-style of the 12 methods)

revise.statement: Session now lazy-loaded on first access instead of at context push (before routing) as in 3.1; process_response still touches ctx.session unconditionally
docs/shell.rst examples broken under new signatures: app.preprocess_request() and app.process_response(app.response_class()) missing ctx argument

docs/shell.rst still refers to test_request_context() as creating a RequestContext (stale naming); docs/api.rst documents the alias correctly; docs/appcontext.rst rewritten with typo 'requet' (line 122)

Signal docstrings removed from signals.py; request_started/request_tearing_down now fired in full_dispatch_request/do_teardown_request (dispatch-bound, not push-bound); docs/signals.rst updated to match
Test-client preserved-context machinery coherent with merged context: preserved contexts popped before each open(), re-pushed after; g persistence inside `with client:` tested
CI: tox matrix 3.10-3.14 + free-threaded (t) + PyPy + tests-min/dev, mypy strict + pyright typing job, uv --locked; pytest filterwarnings=error in pyproject
Python 3.9 dropped (requires-python >=3.10); flask.__version__ removed repo-wide (replacement importlib.metadata)
Robustness gap: __init_subclass__ calls inspect.signature(method) unguarded — signature-mangling decorators on overridden methods can raise at class definition, crashing imports
Import-time DeprecationWarning for every old-style Flask subclass hard-fails user suites running -W error / filterwarnings=error (Flask's own convention); unavoidable per-call-site silencing
External state: upstream main still shows Version 3.2.0 section in CHANGES.rst; 3.2.0 release status after 2025-11-17 Unknown (web_fetch unavailable this session)

hypotheses.statement: This is Flask main at 3.2.0.dev; its defining feature is the merged app/request context refactor (#5639/#5812), which is the primary analysis target

The refactor is architecturally coherent and code-level well-tested; dominant risks are (a) ecosystem blast radius of the context-reuse semantic change + import-time deprecation shim, (b) incomplete docs (broken shell.rst examples), (c) untested old-signature shim path, (d) snapshot CRLF noise; no corrosion — deliberate upstream evolution
